29:45.ar: ٱتۡلُ مَآ أُوحِيَ إِلَيۡكَ مِنَ ٱلۡكِتَٰبِ وَأَقِمِ ٱلصَّلَوٰةَۖ إِنَّ ٱلصَّلَوٰةَ تَنۡهَىٰ عَنِ ٱلۡفَحۡشَآءِ وَٱلۡمُنكَرِۗ وَلَذِكۡرُ ٱللَّهِ أَكۡبَرُۗ وَٱللَّهُ يَعۡلَمُ مَا تَصۡنَعُونَ
29:45.en: Recite that which hath been inspired in thee of the Scripture, and establish worship. Lo! worship preserveth from lewdness and iniquity, but verily remembrance of Allah is more important. And Allah knoweth what ye do

29:46.ar: ۞وَلَا تُجَٰدِلُوٓاْ أَهۡلَ ٱلۡكِتَٰبِ إِلَّا بِٱلَّتِي هِيَ أَحۡسَنُ إِلَّا ٱلَّذِينَ ظَلَمُواْ مِنۡهُمۡۖ وَقُولُوٓاْ ءَامَنَّا بِٱلَّذِيٓ أُنزِلَ إِلَيۡنَا وَأُنزِلَ إِلَيۡكُمۡ وَإِلَٰهُنَا وَإِلَٰهُكُمۡ وَٰحِدࣱ وَنَحۡنُ لَهُۥ مُسۡلِمُونَ
29:46.en: And argue not with the People of the Scripture unless it be in (a way) that is better, save with such of them as do wrong; and say: We believe in that which hath been revealed unto us and revealed unto you; our Allah and your Allah is One, and unto Him we surrender

29:6.ar: وَمَن جَٰهَدَ فَإِنَّمَا يُجَٰهِدُ لِنَفۡسِهِۦٓۚ إِنَّ ٱللَّهَ لَغَنِيٌّ عَنِ ٱلۡعَٰلَمِينَ
29:6.en: And whosoever striveth, striveth only for himself, for lo! Allah is altogether Independent of (His) creatures

29:2.ar: أَحَسِبَ ٱلنَّاسُ أَن يُتۡرَكُوٓاْ أَن يَقُولُوٓاْ ءَامَنَّا وَهُمۡ لَا يُفۡتَنُونَ
29:2.en: Do men imagine that they will be left (at ease) because they say, We believe, and will not be tested with affliction

29:3.ar: وَلَقَدۡ فَتَنَّا ٱلَّذِينَ مِن قَبۡلِهِمۡۖ فَلَيَعۡلَمَنَّ ٱللَّهُ ٱلَّذِينَ صَدَقُواْ وَلَيَعۡلَمَنَّ ٱلۡكَٰذِبِينَ
29:3.en: Lo! We tested those who were before you. Thus Allah knoweth those who are sincere, and knoweth those who feign

29:41.ar: مَثَلُ ٱلَّذِينَ ٱتَّخَذُواْ مِن دُونِ ٱللَّهِ أَوۡلِيَآءَ كَمَثَلِ ٱلۡعَنكَبُوتِ ٱتَّخَذَتۡ بَيۡتࣰ اۖ وَإِنَّ أَوۡهَنَ ٱلۡبُيُوتِ لَبَيۡتُ ٱلۡعَنكَبُوتِۚ لَوۡ كَانُواْ يَعۡلَمُونَ
29:41.en: The likeness of those who choose other patrons than Allah is as the likeness of the spider when she taketh unto herself a house, and lo! the frailest of all houses is the spider's house, if they but knew

29:47.ar: وَكَذَٰلِكَ أَنزَلۡنَآ إِلَيۡكَ ٱلۡكِتَٰبَۚ فَٱلَّذِينَ ءَاتَيۡنَٰهُمُ ٱلۡكِتَٰبَ يُؤۡمِنُونَ بِهِۦۖ وَمِنۡ هَٰٓؤُلَآءِ مَن يُؤۡمِنُ بِهِۦۚ وَمَا يَجۡحَدُ بِـَٔايَٰتِنَآ إِلَّا ٱلۡكَٰفِرُونَ
29:47.en: In like manner We have revealed unto thee the Scripture, and those unto whom We gave the Scripture aforetime will believe therein; and of these (also) there are some who believe therein. And none deny Our revelations save the disbelievers

29:69.ar: وَٱلَّذِينَ جَٰهَدُواْ فِينَا لَنَهۡدِيَنَّهُمۡ سُبُلَنَاۚ وَإِنَّ ٱللَّهَ لَمَعَ ٱلۡمُحۡسِنِينَ
29:69.en: As for those who strive in Us, We surely guide them to Our paths, and lo! Allah is with the good

93:11.en: Therefor of the bounty of thy Lord be thy discourse

29:11.ar: وَلَيَعۡلَمَنَّ ٱللَّهُ ٱلَّذِينَ ءَامَنُواْ وَلَيَعۡلَمَنَّ ٱلۡمُنَٰفِقِينَ
29:11.en: Verily Allah knoweth those who believe, and verily He knoweth the hypocrites

17:32.ar: وَلَا تَقۡرَبُواْ ٱلزِّنَىٰٓۖ إِنَّهُۥ كَانَ فَٰحِشَةࣰ وَسَآءَ سَبِيلࣰ ا
17:32.en: And come not near unto adultery. Lo! it is an abomination and an evil way

9:84.ar: وَلَا تُصَلِّ عَلَىٰٓ أَحَدࣲ مِّنۡهُم مَّاتَ أَبَدࣰ ا وَلَا تَقُمۡ عَلَىٰ قَبۡرِهِۦٓۖ إِنَّهُمۡ كَفَرُواْ بِٱللَّهِ وَرَسُولِهِۦ وَمَاتُواْ وَهُمۡ فَٰسِقُونَ
9:84.en: And never (O Muhammad) pray for one of them who dieth, nor stand by his grave. Lo! they disbelieved in Allah and His messenger, and they died while they were evil-doers

9:103.ar: خُذۡ مِنۡ أَمۡوَٰلِهِمۡ صَدَقَةࣰ تُطَهِّرُهُمۡ وَتُزَكِّيهِم بِهَا وَصَلِّ عَلَيۡهِمۡۖ إِنَّ صَلَوٰتَكَ سَكَنࣱ لَّهُمۡۗ وَٱللَّهُ سَمِيعٌ عَلِيمٌ
9:103.en: Take alms of their wealth, wherewith thou mayst purify them and mayst make them grow, and pray for them. Lo! thy prayer is an assuagement for them. Allah is Hearer, Knower

2:165.ar: وَمِنَ ٱلنَّاسِ مَن يَتَّخِذُ مِن دُونِ ٱللَّهِ أَندَادࣰ ا يُحِبُّونَهُمۡ كَحُبِّ ٱللَّهِۖ وَٱلَّذِينَ ءَامَنُوٓاْ أَشَدُّ حُبࣰّ ا لِّلَّهِۗ وَلَوۡ يَرَى ٱلَّذِينَ ظَلَمُوٓاْ إِذۡ يَرَوۡنَ ٱلۡعَذَابَ أَنَّ ٱلۡقُوَّةَ لِلَّهِ جَمِيعࣰ ا وَأَنَّ ٱللَّهَ شَدِيدُ ٱلۡعَذَابِ
2:165.en: Yet of mankind are some who take unto themselves (objects of worship which they set as) rivals to Allah, loving them with a love like (that which is the due) of Allah (only) - those who believe are stauncher in their love for Allah - Oh, that those who do evil had but known, (on the day) when they behold the doom, that power belongeth wholly to Allah, and that Allah is severe in punishment

2:245.ar: مَّن ذَا ٱلَّذِي يُقۡرِضُ ٱللَّهَ قَرۡضًا حَسَنࣰ ا فَيُضَٰعِفَهُۥ لَهُۥٓ أَضۡعَافࣰ ا كَثِيرَةࣰۚ وَٱللَّهُ يَقۡبِضُ وَيَبۡصُۜطُ وَإِلَيۡهِ تُرۡجَعُونَ
2:245.en: Who is it that will lend unto Allah a goodly loan, so that He may give it increase manifold? Allah straiteneth and enlargeth. Unto Him ye will return

18:54.ar: وَلَقَدۡ صَرَّفۡنَا فِي هَٰذَا ٱلۡقُرۡءَانِ لِلنَّاسِ مِن كُلِّ مَثَلࣲۚ وَكَانَ ٱلۡإِنسَٰنُ أَكۡثَرَ شَيۡءࣲ جَدَلࣰ ا
18:54.en: And verily We have displayed for mankind in this Qur'an all manner of similitudes, but man is more than anything contentious

25:63.ar: وَعِبَادُ ٱلرَّحۡمَٰنِ ٱلَّذِينَ يَمۡشُونَ عَلَى ٱلۡأَرۡضِ هَوۡنࣰ ا وَإِذَا خَاطَبَهُمُ ٱلۡجَٰهِلُونَ قَالُواْ سَلَٰمࣰ ا
25:63.en: The (faithful) slaves of the Beneficent are they who walk upon the earth modestly, and when the foolish ones address them answer: Peace

60:8.ar: لَّا يَنۡهَىٰكُمُ ٱللَّهُ عَنِ ٱلَّذِينَ لَمۡ يُقَٰتِلُوكُمۡ فِي ٱلدِّينِ وَلَمۡ يُخۡرِجُوكُم مِّن دِيَٰرِكُمۡ أَن تَبَرُّوهُمۡ وَتُقۡسِطُوٓاْ إِلَيۡهِمۡۚ إِنَّ ٱللَّهَ يُحِبُّ ٱلۡمُقۡسِطِينَ
60:8.en: Allah forbiddeth you not those who warred not against you on account of religion and drove you not out from your homes, that ye should show them kindness and deal justly with them. Lo! Allah loveth the just dealers

lztBOq9wKDQ.speaker_note: his Friday Arabic tafsir circle continuing Surat Al-Ankabut from verse 45
lztBOq9wKDQ.title: Friday Arabic Tafsir: Surat Al-Ankabut 45-46
lztBOq9wKDQ.one_line: Tools for striving through life: recite the Book, establish prayer, keep Allah constantly in mind, and debate People of the Book only in the best way.
lztBOq9wKDQ.summary: He restates the surah's message: whatever comes, ease or hardship, is the same thing, a test, so the believer's response should be the same, striving: gratitude in practice when given, patience when deprived. Interpreting events as luck, envy or magic leads to inconsistent responses. Before any instruction the Quran fixes understanding, since someone who prays yet wrongs his wife or seizes his siblings' inheritance has simply not understood. The commands of verse 45 follow. Reciting the Book gives guidance, the greatest blessing, answering questions no human experiment could settle. Prayer must be established, not merely performed: like a structure it needs pillars of congregation, learning, sincerity, presence and Quran memorised, and then it holds one back from indecency and wrong. He cites the Prophet's long night prayers and early scholars who completed the Quran in one rak'ah. Remembrance of Allah is greater still, because it is the goal of recitation and prayer: a constant awareness in every step, the food of the soul, without which religion becomes mechanical. Verse 46 tells the Muslims, about to meet Jews in Madinah, to avoid argument, debate only in the best way, never treat decent neighbours harshly, and not debate oppressors such as those who took Palestine by force.

outline.heading: Life as testing and continuous striving
outline.gist: He resumes at verse 45: our relationship with time is testing, and with it, continuous striving.

outline.heading: Two wrong expectations of life
outline.gist: Expecting only good leads to bitter disappointment; seeing only bad ('my luck is always bad') is equally wrong.

outline.heading: Gratitude in action, patience in hardship
outline.gist: Praise is verbal contentment; shukr is using what Allah gave in His pleasure and service of people.

outline.heading: One source, so one response
outline.gist: Everything is a test, so the response should always be striving; reading events as cleverness, envy or magic breeds inconsistent reactions.

outline.heading: Striving in this Makkan surah
outline.gist: Jihad here cannot mean fighting; share blessings of knowledge, money and rank, and be patient through constriction.

outline.heading: First: understanding before action
outline.gist: The Quran fixes the concept before giving practical advice; the spider parable came first.

outline.heading: Praying while wronging one's family
outline.gist: One who reads Quran and prays yet oppresses his wife and takes his siblings' inheritance has not understood, and drives people from religion.

outline.heading: Misreading wealth and deprivation
outline.gist: Wealth is not for touring and photos, and illness is not 'bad luck'; the rich who think Allah gave to the clever try to control others.

outline.heading: Al-Ankabut challenges our understanding
outline.gist: Its opening question mocks the notion of believing without trials; a person first discovers the truth about himself.

outline.heading: Recap: the spider's house
outline.gist: Relying on anyone but Allah is the spider proud of a web a child's broom destroys.

outline.heading: Recite the Book: guidance is the greatest blessing
outline.gist: Allah did not send us into life without a manual; we ask for guidance at least seventeen times a day.

outline.heading: Revelation answers what experiment cannot
outline.gist: Humanity cannot run two-century trials on whether marriage or promiscuity is better; Allah tells us 'do not approach zina'.

outline.heading: Why be honest and eat halal when others prosper?
outline.gist: Because Allah told us it is best in this world and the next; guidance is beyond any price.

outline.heading: Second: establish the prayer
outline.gist: The Quran almost always commands prayer with 'establish', apart from the funeral prayer and praying for those giving charity.

outline.heading: Prayer as a structure with purposes
outline.gist: One establishes only what has a structure and goals; its pillars must be set so it achieves what Allah intends.

outline.heading: Fahsha versus munkar
outline.gist: Fahsha are sins of honour and sexuality; munkar are the other wrongs all people recognise, like killing, theft and lying.

outline.heading: 'I have prayed 25 years and it does not stop me'
outline.gist: Establishing prayer means congregation, learning, sincerity, presence of heart and memorised Quran; time in the masjid alone keeps you from sin.

outline.heading: The fault is the user, not the tool
outline.gist: A rushed, pecking prayer alone in one's room is like a device never plugged in; the user did not read the manual.

outline.heading: Tazkiyah lessons exist to improve your prayer
outline.gist: All the circles of spiritual training aim to help you focus and address Allah with your heart.

outline.heading: The 'majdhub': drawn to Allah without much learning
outline.gist: Some with little fiqh are wholly present in prayer while the learned cannot focus three minutes; people mock what they cannot feel.

outline.heading: Prayer surrounds you with people who call to repentance
outline.gist: The Prophet's last advice was 'the prayer, the prayer'.

outline.heading: 'Give us rest through it, Bilal'
outline.gist: Prayer was relief from the world's worries, which is why he could stand for hours.

outline.heading: A night prayer with the Prophet
outline.gist: Al-Baqarah, An-Nisa and Aal-Imran in one rak'ah, pausing at Paradise and Hell; a Companion was tempted to sit and leave him.

outline.heading: The whole Quran in one rak'ah
outline.gist: Uthman and early scholars like Al-Nakha'i, Al-Sha'bi, Abu Hanifa and Hasan al-Basri did so; his own eleven-hour attempt one Arafah night showed it needs love.

outline.heading: Third: remembrance of Allah is greater
outline.gist: Dhikr is the aim of both recitation and prayer, so it is greater than both.

outline.heading: Dhikr as constant presence
outline.gist: Not only a daily litany: asking at each step whether this pleases Him, and reminding people of their Lord rather than muttering about them.

outline.heading: Better than spending gold and meeting the enemy
outline.gist: The Prophet named remembrance the best and purest deed, because it is the spirit of all other deeds.

outline.heading: Allah does not dwell in a heart full of desires
outline.gist: Believers love Allah more than anything; you cannot strive through life if He is absent from your heart.

outline.heading: Religion without love becomes mechanical
outline.gist: Once love and remembrance left people's understanding, what remained were motions done from custom, fear of scandal or conscience.

outline.heading: Why Ramadan is longed for
outline.gist: Allah lifts some veils, so even a distant person tastes something in a prayer, a sajdah or a recitation.

outline.heading: The soul's food is nearness to Allah
outline.gist: A starved soul dies: feelings dull, no jealousy for honour or religion, only animal pleasures remain.

outline.heading: The worst vessel is the stomach
outline.gist: Filling the body empties the soul; he jokes that some would gladly abrogate this hadith before a mansaf.

outline.heading: All of religion serves remembrance
outline.gist: Every prohibition, prayer, zakah, fast and Hajj exists to help you remember Him, and He remembers those who remember Him.

outline.heading: Draw near a handspan, He draws near an arm's length
outline.gist: His allies have Him present always; they do good to people to please Allah, lending Him a goodly loan.

outline.heading: 'Allah knows what you craft'
outline.gist: San'ah is ordered steps toward a goal: Allah sees how you arranged your life and whether your aims are Him or others disguised as Him.

outline.heading: Summary of the first three tools
outline.gist: Understand from the Book, keep prayer's pillars standing, and keep Allah present in your heart.

outline.heading: Recitation: arguing with the People of the Book
outline.gist: He recites verses 46-47.

outline.heading: Fourth: prepared for Madinah's People of the Book
outline.gist: Revealed between the two pledges of Aqabah, when the Prophet knew he would meet Jews and Christians he had not dealt with in Makkah.

outline.heading: Avoid argument; the wise argue less
outline.gist: Two successive exceptions; heavy arguing drains blessing and striving, and when the ignorant address them, the righteous say peace.

outline.heading: 'In the best way': bring people closer
outline.gist: If you must argue, choose the most moving words and show how little separates them from Islam.

outline.heading: Except the wrongdoers: law or force, not debate
outline.gist: One who wronged you and took your wealth meets the law where there is law; some Muslims wrongly turn rude to decent non-Muslims.

outline.heading: Kindness to neighbours who do not fight you
outline.gist: Those who did not fight you or expel you deserve goodness and fairness, not harshness from a fellow resident.

outline.heading: No debate with those who took Palestine by force
outline.gist: An oppressor uses argument only to stall; Palestine was taken with guns, not debate.

outline.heading: Know whom you are debating
outline.gist: Debate gently with one who misunderstands the cause; with the usurper there is no discussion.

outline.heading: 'Our God and your God is one'
outline.gist: Gather rather than divide: one who embraces Islam keeps his culture and the prophets he loved, receiving their original message.

outline.heading: How the Prophet applied it in Madinah
outline.gist: He treated them well while they were friendly, and expelled them without further debate when they betrayed him.

outline.heading: Outro

16:91.ar: وَأَوۡفُواْ بِعَهۡدِ ٱللَّهِ إِذَا عَٰهَدتُّمۡ وَلَا تَنقُضُواْ ٱلۡأَيۡمَٰنَ بَعۡدَ تَوۡكِيدِهَا وَقَدۡ جَعَلۡتُمُ ٱللَّهَ عَلَيۡكُمۡ كَفِيلًاۚ إِنَّ ٱللَّهَ يَعۡلَمُ مَا تَفۡعَلُونَ
16:91.en: Fulfil the covenant of Allah when ye have covenanted, and break not your oaths after the asseveration of them, and after ye have made Allah surety over you. Lo! Allah knoweth what ye do

48:10.ar: إِنَّ ٱلَّذِينَ يُبَايِعُونَكَ إِنَّمَا يُبَايِعُونَ ٱللَّهَ يَدُ ٱللَّهِ فَوۡقَ أَيۡدِيهِمۡۚ فَمَن نَّكَثَ فَإِنَّمَا يَنكُثُ عَلَىٰ نَفۡسِهِۦۖ وَمَنۡ أَوۡفَىٰ بِمَا عَٰهَدَ عَلَيۡهُ ٱللَّهَ فَسَيُؤۡتِيهِ أَجۡرًا عَظِيمࣰ ا
48:10.en: Lo! those who swear allegiance unto thee (Muhammad), swear allegiance only unto Allah. The Hand of Allah is above their hands. So whosoever breaketh his oath, breaketh it only to his soul's hurt; while whosoever keepeth his covenant with Allah, on him will He bestow immense reward

9:111.ar: ۞إِنَّ ٱللَّهَ ٱشۡتَرَىٰ مِنَ ٱلۡمُؤۡمِنِينَ أَنفُسَهُمۡ وَأَمۡوَٰلَهُم بِأَنَّ لَهُمُ ٱلۡجَنَّةَۚ يُقَٰتِلُونَ فِي سَبِيلِ ٱللَّهِ فَيَقۡتُلُونَ وَيُقۡتَلُونَۖ وَعۡدًا عَلَيۡهِ حَقࣰّ ا فِي ٱلتَّوۡرَىٰةِ وَٱلۡإِنجِيلِ وَٱلۡقُرۡءَانِۚ وَمَنۡ أَوۡفَىٰ بِعَهۡدِهِۦ مِنَ ٱللَّهِۚ فَٱسۡتَبۡشِرُواْ بِبَيۡعِكُمُ ٱلَّذِي بَايَعۡتُم بِهِۦۚ وَذَٰلِكَ هُوَ ٱلۡفَوۡزُ ٱلۡعَظِيمُ
9:111.en: Lo! Allah hath bought from the believers their lives and their wealth because the Garden will be theirs: they shall fight in the way of Allah and shall slay and be slain. It is a promise which is binding on Him in the Torah and the Gospel and the Qur'an. Who fulfilleth His covenant better than Allah? Rejoice then in your bargain that ye have made, for that is the supreme triumph

LFucBWvUwIQ.title: The Pledge of Al-Aqabah: An Offering and a Return
LFucBWvUwIQ.one_line: Muslims today lack a pledge; the Ansar's Second Aqabah oath, given in exchange for Paradise and kept until death, is the standard to hold ourselves to.
LFucBWvUwIQ.summary: Opening with 16:91 on fulfilling covenants, the sheikh admits that fourteen months into the Gaza war he no longer cares what others think of his opinions. He once hoped different cultures could live in mutual respect, but governments have turned a blind eye to Muslim suffering for decades, and only Muslims seem held to any standard. He found the campus encampments across North America refreshing and says Muslims have lacked courage and must speak louder. What is missing, he argues, is a pledge: a standard every Muslim holds themselves to. He narrates the Second Pledge of Aqabah: the terms of hearing and obeying in ease and hardship, spending, commanding good, speaking for Allah without fear of blame, and protecting the Prophet as they protect their own families. Al-Bara' ibn Ma'rur accepts, Abu al-Haytham asks whether the Prophet will abandon them after victory, and the Prophet answers that their blood is his blood. As'ad ibn Zurarah warns of the cost, and when they ask what they get, the answer is Paradise. In the second khutbah, with 9:111, he describes the Ansar racing to pledge and all 72 dying for Allah within thirty years, and asks whether we will pledge the same, committing without waiting for permission or validation.

outline.heading: Opening
No longer caring what they think
outline.gist: Fourteen or fifteen months into the war, even as a teacher of Islamic studies who spends his time on courage and bravery, he admits he no longer cares at all what others think of his views. He once hoped different cultures could live together in harmony and deep mutual respect, but that hope has gone.

outline.heading: A blind eye for decades, and a standard for Muslims only
outline.gist: The way every government has dealt with this sends him back decades: a blind eye has long been turned to Muslim pain and bloodshed. It is naive to expect anyone to care for us more than we care for ourselves, but he thought everyone here was held to one standard, and only Muslims are.

outline.heading: The encampments: we have lacked courage
outline.gist: Good has come of it: students camping on campuses across North America was refreshing, and universities gave in to some of their demands. We have lacked courage and must speak louder and more clearly about what we believe and demand.

outline.heading: We are lacking a pledge
outline.gist: That makes the topic more urgent: the ummah lacks a pledge, a standard that every Muslim in the room and across the globe owes themselves and Allah. The opening verse, 16:91, commands keeping covenants with Allah.

outline.heading: The terms of the pledge
outline.gist: He gives the articles together: hearing and obeying in energy and reluctance, spending in ease and hardship, commanding good and forbidding evil, standing for Allah without fearing anyone's blame, and protecting the Prophet as they protect their own families and wealth.

outline.heading: Al-Bara' ibn Ma'rur: a people of war
outline.gist: Al-Bara' ibn Ma'rur stood and swore by the One who sent him with the truth that they would protect him as they protect their families, for they were a people of war who had inherited it generation after generation.

outline.heading: Abu al-Haytham: will you leave us after victory?
outline.gist: Abu al-Haytham said they were cutting their ties with other peoples: if Allah gave him victory, would he leave them and return to his people? The Prophet answered: blood for blood, ruin for ruin, I am of you and you are of me, I make peace with whom you make peace and war on whom you war.

outline.heading: Their pledge was to Allah Himself
outline.gist: He would live and die with them, and the people cried takbir. Al-Fath 48:10: those who pledge to the Prophet pledge to Allah, whose hand is above their hands, like hands stacked on top of each other in agreement; Allah was giving them the one He loves most on earth.

outline.heading: As'ad ibn Zurarah's warning
outline.gist: As'ad ibn Zurarah told the people of Yathrib to slow down: taking the Prophet meant the enmity of all the Arabs, the killing of their best and the bite of swords. If they could bear it, take him and their reward is with Allah; if they feared for themselves, say so now, which would be more excusable before Allah.

outline.heading: What do we get?
outline.gist: Either you are people of perseverance who take him, or you say now that you cannot. Then they asked: if we do all of this, what do we get? The answer was Paradise.

outline.heading: Interlude
Allah bought their lives and wealth
outline.gist: At-Tawbah 9:111: Allah bought from the believers their lives and wealth in exchange for Paradise, the verse tied to the narration of Abdullah ibn Rawahah at Aqabah. Paradise means beauty in the presence of the Almighty Himself.

outline.heading: Put Islam first
outline.gist: Paradise is access to His compassion, mercy, love, grace and knowledge in ways the human mind cannot begin to grasp. In return you commit to the values and principles of the deen, put Islam first at all times and protect it with your life and wealth; anything less would not be fair to those who gave it.

outline.heading: Lower your hand, As'ad
outline.gist: The Ansar told As'ad to lower his hand: they would never abandon this pledge or ask to be released from it. They raced to pledge as if whoever pledged first would enter Paradise first.

outline.heading: Will you pledge what the Ansar pledged?
outline.gist: O servants of Allah, will you pledge to the Prophet what the Ansar pledged? If you do, he enters your life and never leaves it; it is the best transaction you can make, and nothing has changed since that year.

outline.heading: All 72 died for Allah within thirty years
outline.gist: They stuck to it to the end: over the next thirty years they fell one by one until all 72 who pledged that night had died for the sake of Allah, and they saw Him keep His word. That is what to hope for.

outline.heading: Full commitment always finds a way
outline.gist: Whoever is fully committed, as the Ansar were, always finds a way to push Islam forward and be a force of good, however busy, old, young, sick or poor, wherever they are dropped in place and time.

outline.heading: No permission, no validation, no excuses
outline.gist: You need no permission, seek no validation, wait for no support and have no excuses for not showing up. This is your cause: you are inside it, not outside looking in.

outline.heading: Outro

29:41.ar: مَثَلُ ٱلَّذِينَ ٱتَّخَذُواْ مِن دُونِ ٱللَّهِ أَوۡلِيَآءَ كَمَثَلِ ٱلۡعَنكَبُوتِ ٱتَّخَذَتۡ بَيۡتࣰ اۖ وَإِنَّ أَوۡهَنَ ٱلۡبُيُوتِ لَبَيۡتُ ٱلۡعَنكَبُوتِۚ لَوۡ كَانُواْ يَعۡلَمُونَ
29:41.en: The likeness of those who choose other patrons than Allah is as the likeness of the spider when she taketh unto herself a house, and lo! the frailest of all houses is the spider's house, if they but knew

29:42.ar: إِنَّ ٱللَّهَ يَعۡلَمُ مَا يَدۡعُونَ مِن دُونِهِۦ مِن شَيۡءࣲۚ وَهُوَ ٱلۡعَزِيزُ ٱلۡحَكِيمُ
29:42.en: Lo! Allah knoweth what thing they invoke instead of Him. He is the Mighty, the Wise

29:43.ar: وَتِلۡكَ ٱلۡأَمۡثَٰلُ نَضۡرِبُهَا لِلنَّاسِۖ وَمَا يَعۡقِلُهَآ إِلَّا ٱلۡعَٰلِمُونَ
29:43.en: As for these similitudes, We coin them for mankind, but none will grasp their meaning save the wise

29:44.ar: خَلَقَ ٱللَّهُ ٱلسَّمَٰوَٰتِ وَٱلۡأَرۡضَ بِٱلۡحَقِّۚ إِنَّ فِي ذَٰلِكَ لَأٓيَةࣰ لِّلۡمُؤۡمِنِينَ
29:44.en: Allah created the heavens and the earth with truth. Lo! therein is indeed a portent for believers

29:45.ar: ٱتۡلُ مَآ أُوحِيَ إِلَيۡكَ مِنَ ٱلۡكِتَٰبِ وَأَقِمِ ٱلصَّلَوٰةَۖ إِنَّ ٱلصَّلَوٰةَ تَنۡهَىٰ عَنِ ٱلۡفَحۡشَآءِ وَٱلۡمُنكَرِۗ وَلَذِكۡرُ ٱللَّهِ أَكۡبَرُۗ وَٱللَّهُ يَعۡلَمُ مَا تَصۡنَعُونَ
29:45.en: Recite that which hath been inspired in thee of the Scripture, and establish worship. Lo! worship preserveth from lewdness and iniquity, but verily remembrance of Allah is more important. And Allah knoweth what ye do

29:2.ar: أَحَسِبَ ٱلنَّاسُ أَن يُتۡرَكُوٓاْ أَن يَقُولُوٓاْ ءَامَنَّا وَهُمۡ لَا يُفۡتَنُونَ
29:2.en: Do men imagine that they will be left (at ease) because they say, We believe, and will not be tested with affliction

29:40.ar: فَكُلًّا أَخَذۡنَا بِذَنۢبِهِۦۖ فَمِنۡهُم مَّنۡ أَرۡسَلۡنَا عَلَيۡهِ حَاصِبࣰ ا وَمِنۡهُم مَّنۡ أَخَذَتۡهُ ٱلصَّيۡحَةُ وَمِنۡهُم مَّنۡ خَسَفۡنَا بِهِ ٱلۡأَرۡضَ وَمِنۡهُم مَّنۡ أَغۡرَقۡنَاۚ وَمَا كَانَ ٱللَّهُ لِيَظۡلِمَهُمۡ وَلَٰكِن كَانُوٓاْ أَنفُسَهُمۡ يَظۡلِمُونَ
29:40.en: So We took each one in his sin; of them was he on whom We sent a hurricane, and of them was he who was overtaken by the (Awful) Cry, and of them was he whom We caused the earth to swallow, and of them was he whom We drowned. It was not for Allah to wrong them, but they wronged themselves

29:6.ar: وَمَن جَٰهَدَ فَإِنَّمَا يُجَٰهِدُ لِنَفۡسِهِۦٓۚ إِنَّ ٱللَّهَ لَغَنِيٌّ عَنِ ٱلۡعَٰلَمِينَ
29:6.en: And whosoever striveth, striveth only for himself, for lo! Allah is altogether Independent of (His) creatures

29:69.ar: وَٱلَّذِينَ جَٰهَدُواْ فِينَا لَنَهۡدِيَنَّهُمۡ سُبُلَنَاۚ وَإِنَّ ٱللَّهَ لَمَعَ ٱلۡمُحۡسِنِينَ
29:69.en: As for those who strive in Us, We surely guide them to Our paths, and lo! Allah is with the good

29:62.ar: ٱللَّهُ يَبۡسُطُ ٱلرِّزۡقَ لِمَن يَشَآءُ مِنۡ عِبَادِهِۦ وَيَقۡدِرُ لَهُۥٓۚ إِنَّ ٱللَّهَ بِكُلِّ شَيۡءٍ عَلِيمࣱ‏
29:62.en: Allah maketh the provision wide for whom He will of His bondmen, and straiteneth it for whom (He will). Lo! Allah is Aware of all things

23:99.ar: حَتَّىٰٓ إِذَا جَآءَ أَحَدَهُمُ ٱلۡمَوۡتُ قَالَ رَبِّ ٱرۡجِعُونِ
23:99.en: Until, when death cometh unto one of them, he saith: My Lord! Send me back

23:100.ar: لَعَلِّيٓ أَعۡمَلُ صَٰلِحࣰ ا فِيمَا تَرَكۡتُۚ كَلَّآۚ إِنَّهَا كَلِمَةٌ هُوَ قَآئِلُهَاۖ وَمِن وَرَآئِهِم بَرۡزَخٌ إِلَىٰ يَوۡمِ يُبۡعَثُونَ
23:100.en: That I may do right in that which I have left behind! But nay! It is but a word that he speaketh; and behind them is a barrier until the day when they are raised

3:140.ar: إِن يَمۡسَسۡكُمۡ قَرۡحࣱ فَقَدۡ مَسَّ ٱلۡقَوۡمَ قَرۡحࣱ مِّثۡلُهُۥۚ وَتِلۡكَ ٱلۡأَيَّامُ نُدَاوِلُهَا بَيۡنَ ٱلنَّاسِ وَلِيَعۡلَمَ ٱللَّهُ ٱلَّذِينَ ءَامَنُواْ وَيَتَّخِذَ مِنكُمۡ شُهَدَآءَۗ وَٱللَّهُ لَا يُحِبُّ ٱلظَّٰلِمِينَ
3:140.en: If ye have received a blow, the (disbelieving) people have received a blow the like thereof. These are (only) the vicissitudes which We cause to follow one another for mankind, to the end that Allah may know those who believe and may choose witnesses from among you; and Allah loveth not wrong-doers

3:141.ar: وَلِيُمَحِّصَ ٱللَّهُ ٱلَّذِينَ ءَامَنُواْ وَيَمۡحَقَ ٱلۡكَٰفِرِينَ
3:141.en: And that Allah may prove those who believe, and may blight the disbelievers

2:216.ar: كُتِبَ عَلَيۡكُمُ ٱلۡقِتَالُ وَهُوَ كُرۡهࣱ لَّكُمۡۖ وَعَسَىٰٓ أَن تَكۡرَهُواْ شَيۡـࣰٔ ا وَهُوَ خَيۡرࣱ لَّكُمۡۖ وَعَسَىٰٓ أَن تُحِبُّواْ شَيۡـࣰٔ ا وَهُوَ شَرࣱّ لَّكُمۡۚ وَٱللَّهُ يَعۡلَمُ وَأَنتُمۡ لَا تَعۡلَمُونَ
2:216.en: Warfare is ordained for you, though it is hateful unto you; but it may happen that ye hate a thing which is good for you, and it may happen that ye love a thing which is bad for you. Allah knoweth, ye know not

2:217.ar: يَسۡـَٔلُونَكَ عَنِ ٱلشَّهۡرِ ٱلۡحَرَامِ قِتَالࣲ فِيهِۖ قُلۡ قِتَالࣱ فِيهِ كَبِيرࣱۚ وَصَدٌّ عَن سَبِيلِ ٱللَّهِ وَكُفۡرُۢ بِهِۦ وَٱلۡمَسۡجِدِ ٱلۡحَرَامِ وَإِخۡرَاجُ أَهۡلِهِۦ مِنۡهُ أَكۡبَرُ عِندَ ٱللَّهِۚ وَٱلۡفِتۡنَةُ أَكۡبَرُ مِنَ ٱلۡقَتۡلِۗ وَلَا يَزَالُونَ يُقَٰتِلُونَكُمۡ حَتَّىٰ يَرُدُّوكُمۡ عَن دِينِكُمۡ إِنِ ٱسۡتَطَٰعُواْۚ وَمَن يَرۡتَدِدۡ مِنكُمۡ عَن دِينِهِۦ فَيَمُتۡ وَهُوَ كَافِرࣱ فَأُوْلَٰٓئِكَ حَبِطَتۡ أَعۡمَٰلُهُمۡ فِي ٱلدُّنۡيَا وَٱلۡأٓخِرَةِۖ وَأُوْلَٰٓئِكَ أَصۡحَٰبُ ٱلنَّارِۖ هُمۡ فِيهَا خَٰلِدُونَ
2:217.en: They question thee (O Muhammad) with regard to warfare in the sacred month. Say: Warfare therein is a great (transgression), but to turn (men) from the way of Allah, and to disbelieve in Him and in the Inviolable Place of Worship, and to expel His people thence, is a greater with Allah; for persecution is worse than killing. And they will not cease from fighting against you till they have made you renegades from your religion, if they can. And whoso becometh a renegade and dieth in his disbelief: such are they whose works have fallen both in the world and the Hereafter. Such are rightful owners of the Fire: they will abide therein

2:190.ar: وَقَٰتِلُواْ فِي سَبِيلِ ٱللَّهِ ٱلَّذِينَ يُقَٰتِلُونَكُمۡ وَلَا تَعۡتَدُوٓاْۚ إِنَّ ٱللَّهَ لَا يُحِبُّ ٱلۡمُعۡتَدِينَ
2:190.en: Fight in the way of Allah against those who fight against you, but begin not hostilities. Lo! Allah loveth not aggressors

4:77.en: Hast thou not seen those unto whom it was said: Withhold your hands, establish worship and pay the poordue, but when fighting was prescribed for them behold! a party of them fear mankind even as their fear of Allah or with greater fear, and say: Our Lord! Why hast Thou ordained fighting for us? If only Thou wouldst give us respite yet a while! Say (unto them, O Muhammad): The comfort of this world is scant; the Hereafter will be better for him who wardeth off (evil); and ye will not be wronged the down upon a date-stone

89:15.en: As for man, whenever his Lord trieth him by honouring him, and is gracious unto him, he saith: My Lord honoureth me

2:26.en: Lo! Allah disdaineth not to coin the similitude even of a gnat. Those who believe know that it is the truth from their Lord; but those who disbelieve say: What doth Allah wish (to teach) by such a similitude? He misleadeth many thereby, and He guideth many thereby; and He misleadeth thereby only miscreants

20:18.ar: قَالَ هِيَ عَصَايَ أَتَوَكَّؤُاْ عَلَيۡهَا وَأَهُشُّ بِهَا عَلَىٰ غَنَمِي وَلِيَ فِيهَا مَـَٔارِبُ أُخۡرَىٰ

26:14.en: And they have a crime against me, so I fear that they will kill me

20:45.en: They said: Our Lord! Lo! we fear that he may be beforehand with us or that he may play the tyrant

20:46.ar: قَالَ لَا تَخَافَآۖ إِنَّنِي مَعَكُمَآ أَسۡمَعُ وَأَرَىٰ
20:46.en: He said: Fear not. Lo! I am with you twain, Hearing and Seeing

20:67.en: And Moses conceived a fear in his mind

20:68.en: We said: Fear not! Lo! thou art the higher

5:22.ar: قَالُواْ يَٰمُوسَىٰٓ إِنَّ فِيهَا قَوۡمࣰ ا جَبَّارِينَ وَإِنَّا لَن نَّدۡخُلَهَا حَتَّىٰ يَخۡرُجُواْ مِنۡهَا فَإِن يَخۡرُجُواْ مِنۡهَا فَإِنَّا دَٰخِلُونَ
5:22.en: They said: O Moses! Lo! a giant people (dwell) therein and lo! we go not in till they go forth from thence. When they go forth from thence, then we will enter (not till then)

5:23.ar: قَالَ رَجُلَانِ مِنَ ٱلَّذِينَ يَخَافُونَ أَنۡعَمَ ٱللَّهُ عَلَيۡهِمَا ٱدۡخُلُواْ عَلَيۡهِمُ ٱلۡبَابَ فَإِذَا دَخَلۡتُمُوهُ فَإِنَّكُمۡ غَٰلِبُونَۚ وَعَلَى ٱللَّهِ فَتَوَكَّلُوٓاْ إِن كُنتُم مُّؤۡمِنِينَ
5:23.en: Then out spake two of those who feared (their Lord, men) unto whom Allah had been gracious: Enter in upon them by the gate, for if ye enter by it, lo! ye will be victorious. So put your trust (in Allah) if ye are indeed believers

38:27.ar: وَمَا خَلَقۡنَا ٱلسَّمَآءَ وَٱلۡأَرۡضَ وَمَا بَيۡنَهُمَا بَٰطِلࣰ اۚ ذَٰلِكَ ظَنُّ ٱلَّذِينَ كَفَرُواْۚ فَوَيۡلࣱ لِّلَّذِينَ كَفَرُواْ مِنَ ٱلنَّارِ
38:27.en: And We created not the heaven and the earth and all that is between them in vain. That is the opinion of those who disbelieve. And woe unto those who disbelieve, from the Fire

mrv0S-sfb8g.title: Friday Arabic Tafsir: Surat Al-Ankabut 41-45
mrv0S-sfb8g.one_line: Life as mujahadah, the parable of the spider's house for anyone who relies on other than Allah, and the first command: recite the Book.
mrv0S-sfb8g.summary: He sums up the surah so far: everyone is tested, and the believer's way of meeting time is mujahadah, striving toward a goal despite hardship, which he distinguishes from patience, forbearance and fighting, terms the Quran keeps apart. Trials come through giving as well as withholding, and the Companions feared the days of wealth more than the days of hardship. This world is a house of testing, not reward; there is no negotiating with Allah or with time, and one strives with whatever one is given. He then opens the third section with the central verse that names the surah. Whoever takes allies besides Allah is like a spider: its silk is the strongest natural material, produced from its own body, yet its house is the frailest, and the spider has no idea how weak it is. Humans, whose strength comes entirely from outside, are weaker still, so leaning on money, rank, connections or power is the spider's mistake. He uses the advice to Ibn Abbas, Pharaoh's fall and Musa's staff to show Allah is the only true support, and the creation of the heavens and earth with truth as a call to stand with truth. The section's first practical command is to recite and study the Quran.

outline.heading: Section one recap: tested whether you believe or not
outline.gist: No one can believe and escape being tested; the way through is striving for Allah.

outline.heading: Mujahadah versus patience and forbearance
outline.gist: Forbearance is not getting angry when provoked, patience is persisting in one's habits, and jihad is pushing toward a goal despite hardship.

outline.heading: Every prophet in section two emigrated
outline.gist: Ibrahim, Lut and Shu'ayb strove with their peoples, then left them; section three gives the commands for striving.

outline.heading: Tested by giving as well as by withholding
outline.gist: People fear poverty and illness but rarely the trial of wealth, rank, children and position, which ruins more people.

outline.heading: Companions who missed the days of hardship
outline.gist: After the conquests, many saw their prosperity as a trial and longed for the poor, persecuted days with the Prophet.

outline.heading: This world is a house of testing, not reward
outline.gist: Trials will find you wherever you run; demanding that the world be a place of reward is ignorance.

outline.heading: Wanting reward here and work later
outline.gist: Man wants reward in this life and then asks on the Day to be sent back to do good deeds.

outline.heading: Days alternate: strive with whatever you are given
outline.gist: Set the goal of meeting Allah pleased with you; strive with health, with illness, with the Quran, or against fear and poverty.

outline.heading: Jihad and qital are distinct in the Quran
outline.gist: Verses on fighting use qital explicitly; this Makkan surah uses jihad, and 'the peak of the matter is jihad' refers to the broad sense.

outline.heading: Meeting the world head-on
outline.gist: Ease is not honour and restriction is not humiliation; both are tests, met by striving in da'wah, truth and obedience.

outline.heading: No negotiating with Allah or with time
outline.gist: You have nothing to bargain with; time does not stop or rewind for anyone, so wasted years stay wasted.

outline.heading: The prophets as models of striving
outline.gist: Ibrahim was burned, exiled and long deprived of children; compare yourself before complaining.

outline.heading: Shu'ayb, Hud, Salih and Musa
outline.gist: Each faced a hostile people; perhaps your trials are harder than the prophets', he says wryly.

outline.heading: 'Each We seized for his sin': tyrants fall unplanned
outline.gist: The oppressors are between Allah's fingers and fall when He wills; your only task is to strive for Him.

outline.heading: Truthfulness shows when it is hard
outline.gist: Saying you passed when you passed proves nothing; honesty shows when you failed. A life of ease proves nothing about devotion.

outline.heading: Section three: divine commands worth memorising
outline.gist: From verse 41 to the end the passage deserves to be memorised and pondered.

outline.heading: Recitation of the parable of the spider
outline.gist: He recites verses 41-44.

outline.heading: What a wali is
outline.gist: An ally is whoever you take to support, back and help you.

outline.heading: No ally but Allah in your striving
outline.gist: If your reassurance about yourself, your future or your children rests on anyone other than Allah, you are like the spider.

outline.heading: Lessons from the smallest creatures
outline.gist: Allah is not shy to strike a parable of a gnat or smaller; much human invention came from observing creation.

outline.heading: Spider silk: strongest material, made from its own body
outline.gist: Its silk is stronger than steel of equal thickness and traps every creature of its size.

outline.heading: The spider cannot see beyond its world
outline.gist: It knows nothing of elephants or humans and spends what are years of its short life perfecting a house it trusts.

outline.heading: Humans are weaker than the spider
outline.gist: A spider our size would overpower us; our strength comes entirely from outside our bodies.

outline.heading: How Allah sees us relying on a bank balance
outline.gist: As we look at a spider proud of its web until a broom or a child's foot ends it, so is one who leans on money, rank or status.

outline.heading: Our place in the cosmos
outline.gist: A passing star could burn a whole galaxy; knowing our weakness, the answer is reliance on Allah while striving.

outline.heading: Strongest material, frailest house
outline.gist: The Quran calls the house frailest though its material is strongest; the stronger you are by other than Allah, the easier your ruin.

outline.heading: 'Allah knows whatever they call upon': not only idols
outline.gist: The wording is general: anything you believe benefits you apart from Allah.

outline.heading: The advice to Ibn Abbas
outline.gist: If the whole nation gathered to benefit or harm you, they could only do what Allah wrote; the pens are lifted, so stop fretting.

outline.heading: Hidden reliance on other than Allah
outline.gist: The idol-worshipper admits his idol; others secretly rely on wealth, connections, rank or power without confessing it.

outline.heading: Al-'Aziz: why take the abased as an ally?
outline.gist: Everything below the Mighty is lowly; calling on another is a drowning man calling on another drowning man.

outline.heading: Only those who know understand the parables
outline.gist: The spider has more reason than us to feel strong and independent, yet its house is frailest; we are the same if we rely on others.

outline.heading: Rulers who think they cannot be moved
outline.gist: Like a web blown away by wind, a man on his throne can fall by less.

outline.heading: Interlude
Pharaoh's power and today's tyrant
outline.gist: No one on earth was stronger than Pharaoh, who enslaved people openly; only Musa stood up to him.

outline.heading: Musa's staff: Allah uses what is in your hand
outline.gist: To every fear Allah answered 'take your staff'; with it Pharaoh was defeated and the sea split, without outside means.

outline.heading: The Amalekites and Musa's lesson
outline.gist: Musa learned to enter when commanded despite giants at the gate; Bani Isra'il did not learn the lesson.

outline.heading: Stop worrying about what you cannot change
outline.gist: Understanding the parable means relying on no weak creature and knowing only Allah helps you.

outline.heading: Heavens and earth created with truth
outline.gist: Existence stays sound only while truth runs through it; when falsehood prevails it decays, as human life has today.

outline.heading: Then stand with the truth wherever it is
outline.gist: Even if falsehood or a Pharaoh seems stronger, follow truth and resist falsehood with what you have until you meet Allah.

outline.heading: Why this verse closes the parable
outline.gist: Allah did not create the heavens and earth in vain; believers and corrupters will not be treated alike.

outline.heading: Recitation: how to strive
outline.gist: Having grasped that life is trial, the believer asks how to meet it; the commands begin.

outline.heading: First command: tilawah, not just qira'ah
outline.gist: Qira'ah covers study and gathering knowledge broadly; tilawah is voicing the revealed words, as the Prophet recited what Jibril brought.

outline.heading: No way out for the ummah except this Book
outline.gist: You cannot strive for Allah without knowing what He loves and hates; the ummah's revival waits on returning to the Quran.

outline.heading: Outro

PW4TJ2dbTt4.title: There Is God
PW4TJ2dbTt4.one_line: After the fall of Syria's tyrant: faith rests on constants, trials test whether you hold on to it, and hope is a command only for those who work.
PW4TJ2dbTt4.summary: Two weeks after the Syrian regime fell, the sheikh notes that Muslims everywhere rejoiced, proof that people are thirsty for freedom, yet he refuses to let that joy distract from Gaza's ongoing massacre. He explains why he now speaks more bluntly: after fourteen months of his own government's complacency, caution has become complicity, and the hypocrisy must be named. A Syrian friend, a practising Muslim, blurted out when the tyrant fled that it turns out there is a God. From that slip he draws a lesson: Iman is not belief without evidence, as the English word suggests, but certainty built on constants in creation and history, with a personal touch on top that long trials can leave vulnerable. He explains 12:110, where the messengers came close to despair before help arrived, and 2:214, where believers were shaken until they asked when Allah's help would come. The real struggle, he says, is holding on to iman; he saw many Syrians lose faith after 2011 and recalls the drowned child Alan Kurdi, dressed like his own son. In the second khutbah he argues that the Quran forbids despair and commands hope only when you work, illustrated by the Prophet striking the boulder at the trench, and tells young people they are the hope.

outline.heading: Opening
Joy over Syria: a thirst for freedom
outline.gist: He has never seen so much happiness on Muslim faces from every region, nor received so many congratulations, even on Eid. People are thirsty for any removal of oppression; we thought slavery had ended, but only its labels and methods have changed.

outline.heading: No joy should distract from Gaza
outline.gist: After more than 400 days, Gazans are still pulling their children from under the rubble of their homes while the world finds other things to talk about. He cannot in conscience let any joy or victory distract Muslims while people are still being murdered.

outline.heading: Why he now speaks more bluntly
outline.gist: A year ago he weighed every word, out of respect for the country and its unity. After fourteen months of blunt complacency from the government Canadians voted in, while people are killed daily, he feels Muslims must raise their voices and make more noise.

outline.heading: Name the hypocrisy: this is genocide
outline.gist: What the Israeli government is doing is brutality, systematic racism and a genocidal attempt on an indigenous people while the imperial powers watch. The hypocrisy can only run so long; by staying quiet we have enabled and even defended it.

outline.heading: 'It turns out there is a God'
outline.gist: A Syrian friend, a practising Muslim, said it to himself when the news broke that the tyrant had fled, and a doctor's online post reflected on the same phrase. The road to Jerusalem runs through Damascus and Cairo. The slip revealed something deep in a believer's soul: a Muslim builds faith on the constants of the universe.

outline.heading: Iman is not belief without evidence
outline.gist: In English, belief means accepting something with no evidence. Translating iman as belief created a cultural discrepancy, as though Allah asked us to accept Him without proof; that is not what iman is.

outline.heading: The personal touch on top of the constants
outline.gist: All the evidence in the universe, in life and in history points to one Creator, and that is how certainty is reached. Allah also knows the human heart needs a personal experience; an answered dua is that touch on top, not the foundation. For Syrians, a 54-year struggle had worn it thin, and the regime's fall was one of the days of Allah that restored it.

outline.heading: When the messengers nearly despaired
outline.gist: Yusuf 12:110: the messengers came close to despair after a struggle so long that they wondered whether they had been deceived, though they never lost their iman. At that limit Allah's help came, whoever He willed was saved, and His punishment was not held back from the criminals.

outline.heading: Shaken as those before you were
outline.gist: Al-Baqarah 2:214: do you think you will enter Paradise without the trials of those before you? They were struck by hardship and shaken, an earthquake of faith rather than of the ground.

outline.heading: The real struggle is holding on to iman
outline.gist: For Syrians the struggle was not only to remove tyranny but to protect their iman; he personally saw many people lose their faith between 2011 and 2018. Lose everything else and keep your iman and you still have a case before Allah; whatever you face, oppression, poverty or disease, the fight is to hold on.

outline.heading: Alan Kurdi and the disappeared
outline.gist: In 2015 Alan Kurdi washed up on a Greek shore, the same age as his son and wearing the same red shirt and blue shorts. Hundreds of thousands died in intelligence facilities and were disposed of without a trace, leaving families with no closure, asking why.

outline.heading: The explanation will come
outline.gist: When Musa asked Khidr why he holed the boat and killed the boy, Khidr told him the explanation would come; you have to persevere and hold on. The believers in 2:214 were shaken until the Messenger himself asked when Allah's help would come.

outline.heading: Allah's help is near; can you hold on?
outline.gist: Allah's help is very near: removing a tyranny is never difficult for Him and can happen in days. The only question is whether you hold on to the end or lose hope.

outline.heading: Interlude
Despair is forbidden
outline.gist: The Quran hardly uses the word hope, because hope without parameters becomes wishful thinking, a narcotic that numbs you. Instead it forbids the opposite: only disbelievers despair of Allah's relief, and only the astray despair of His mercy.

outline.heading: Hope is commanded when you work
outline.gist: Muslims are commanded to have hope on one condition: that they are putting in effort. Even if you are alone and your effort is tiny against an enormous goal, if you work with all your might you are not merely entitled to hope, you are obliged to have it.

outline.heading: The trench: a boulder and broken morale
outline.gist: As Imam Ahmad narrates, while digging the five-kilometre trench against 10,000 attackers, sleepless and hungry for fifteen days, the companions hit a boulder and brought it to the Prophet. A boulder was nothing to a thousand men; their morale had broken, and he saw it.

outline.heading: Three strikes: Sham, Persia, Yemen
outline.gist: He had water poured on it and struck it three times; with each spark he declared that Sham, Persia and Yemen would be conquered, and a third of the rock crumbled each time. Men too afraid to leave the trench laughed, but he understood the equation: people working hard toward a goal have hope.

outline.heading: You are the hope
outline.gist: It took decades, but those who stood there witnessed the fall of Persia, Rome and Yemen. Young people especially are the hope whether they like it or not, and their conduct decides what that hope looks like.

1fADdLEz570.title: Surat Al-Qalam, Part 6: Verses 48-52
1fADdLEz570.one_line: Perseverance protects one's values: the lesson of Yunus losing patience at the last moment, and how the Prophet's flawless character left his enemies only envy.
1fADdLEz570.summary: Closing Al-Qalam, he explains the one direct command to the Prophet in the surah's last section: be patient for your Lord's judgment. Perseverance is not itself an ethic but the decision that guards all ethics, because life will test every value. He then tells the story of Yunus in detail: beloved by his people, he left them in anger out of love just before the deadline, without permission, and ended in the whale until his sincere admission of wrong. His only error was losing his grit at the last moment and deciding they were beyond hope, which is never a messenger's call. This taught the Prophet never to give up on Quraysh, seen in Umar's conversion and in his treatment of Abu Sufyan at the conquest. The final verses describe the disbelievers' envious stares, wishing he would slip so they could ruin his name; finding no ethical flaw, they could only call him mad. He tells listeners they carry the same burden: their slips will be used against Islam. After prayer he reflects on the hadith that remembrance of Allah is the best deed, since it is the essence that gives charity and sacrifice their worth.

outline.heading: The surah's place and its two requirements
outline.gist: Al-Qalam set out what a Muslim must know and which values he cannot afford to lack; the last piece highlights this in a striking way.

outline.heading: Interlude
The one command: be patient for your Lord's judgment
outline.gist: After telling the Prophet to leave the deniers to Allah, the surah gives its only standalone command, which is what you need to keep your values.

outline.heading: Perseverance is a decision, not an ethic
outline.gist: Honesty and trustworthiness are ethics; perseverance, like striving, is an attitude you choose, and it is how values survive temptation and circumstance.

outline.heading: Why perseverance does not describe Allah
outline.gist: Persevering implies difficulty, and nothing is difficult for Allah, so listing it among His names is linguistically inaccurate.

outline.heading: Without perseverance all your values are lost
outline.gist: Not cheating, not lying, refusing bribes and double standards will be hard, so the command comes paired with an example to avoid.

outline.heading: Yunus: the first prophet named in revelation order
outline.gist: Adam comes first in the mushaf, but in the order of revelation the Prophet first heard of Yunus, and not as praise.

outline.heading: No one may claim to be better than Yunus
outline.gist: The Prophet forbade belittling Yunus; a flaw Allah points out is a lesson, not license to look down on a prophet.

outline.heading: Yunus in Nineveh: rejected but never harmed
outline.gist: His people refused his message yet respected him too much to harm him; each prophet in the Quran adds something new to learn.

outline.heading: The ultimatum and his anger born of love
outline.gist: Told his people had days left, he was upset with them the way one is with a loved one who ruins their own health.

outline.heading: Character that protects a caller
outline.gist: Like a beloved early companion whom Quraysh never persecuted, Yunus's impeccable ethics kept his people from harming him.

outline.heading: Prophets may not leave without permission
outline.gist: Even the Prophet waited for permission to leave Makkah; Yunus left early in anger, which was his mistake.

outline.heading: Abu Bakr's tears at the news of the Hijrah
outline.gist: Abu Bakr kept asking to leave; when told he would accompany the Prophet he wept with joy.

outline.heading: He left in anger, out of love
outline.gist: Yunus's decision came in a moment of anger but out of love for his people; the 'companion of the whale' is named.

outline.heading: Muawiyah and Ibn Abbas: he thought We would not restrict him
outline.gist: The verb comes from the root of restricting, not ability: Yunus thought he would not be held to account, not that Allah lacked power.

outline.heading: The sinking ship and the drawing of lots
outline.gist: His name came up three times though the passengers loved him; he understood the sign and jumped.

outline.heading: His call from the whale while constricted
outline.gist: He declared Allah's oneness and admitted his wrong while in a state of both physical and psychological constriction.

outline.heading: Mercy caught him at the last moment
outline.gist: Had his Lord's blessing not reached him in time he would have been cast onto open land blameworthy; instead he emerged forgiven.

outline.heading: Healing under the tree and return to his people
outline.gist: A broad-leafed plant shaded and healed him, and he was sent back to the hundred thousand of Nineveh.

outline.heading: The broken protocol and Nineveh's repentance
outline.gist: Leaving early halted the usual pattern of punishment; on his return his people reconsidered and Allah accepted their repentance.

outline.heading: His Lord chose him and made him righteous
outline.gist: The verb denotes choosing the best for a good purpose, as the Prophet was chosen from the best lineage.

outline.heading: The mistake to avoid: losing patience at the last minute
outline.gist: His people would have believed within the three days; he lost his perseverance just before the end, which is why mercy had to catch him at the end.

outline.heading: Letting anger in was an ethical lapse
outline.gist: He allowed anger into his heart without enough perseverance to push it back, and would otherwise have repented with his people, not alone.

outline.heading: Grit: you lose only when you stay down
outline.gist: Hold on until it seems useless, then harder; your enemy and life itself bargain on you staying down.

outline.heading: Hold your values and never act from anger
outline.gist: Having understood the legacy of principles, persevere and let nothing shake them; Yunus made his story harder than it needed to be.

outline.heading: The inevitability of faith
outline.gist: Those who will believe will believe; you cannot force people, only hold your ground and not lose hope.

outline.heading: Realizing it was not over
outline.gist: On the ship he saw that his people were still alive and that he had no standing to decide Allah would not accept them.

outline.heading: A true apology requires believing you were wrong
outline.gist: Apologizing for someone's feelings makes it worse; Yunus had to find and own his actual mistake for his words to mean anything.

outline.heading: The belly of the whale as the unexplored self
outline.gist: Trapped where death seemed easier than life, he had to enter the parts of the soul one avoids in order to see where he went wrong.

outline.heading: You are not the judge of who will be forgiven
outline.gist: Leaving almost ruined his people's faith; he confessed he had wronged them by leaving before he was told.

outline.heading: Why the Prophet never lost hope in Quraysh
outline.gist: Despite years of persecution, killing and war, he kept hoping his people would believe because of this lesson.

outline.heading: Umar and his father's donkey
outline.gist: Makkans said Umar would accept Islam only after his father's donkey did, yet he became an anchor of the ummah; never judge who will arrive.

outline.heading: Abu Sufyan at the conquest of Makkah
outline.gist: The Prophet still hoped for Abu Sufyan's faith after everything; Abu Sufyan marvelled at his patience, showing the lesson of Yunus applied.

outline.heading: Interlude
The surah's arc before its final advice
outline.gist: The Prophet's ethics, the sixteen vices, the orchard, the Muslim and the criminal, and perseverance all build to the last verses.

outline.heading: They almost make you slip with their looks
outline.gist: The rare verb means to make something slide; the looking describes envy and frustration wishing he would fall.

outline.heading: Waiting for one mistake to ruin a reputation
outline.gist: To slip figuratively is to make an error they can seize on to tarnish his name.

outline.heading: When they heard the Reminder they called him mad
outline.gist: The Quran shook their status quo, but his character gave them nothing, so they resorted to calling him mad.

outline.heading: The opening disclaimer: you are not mad
outline.gist: The surah opened by denying madness so this ending would not be misread; the Quran's threads come together if you persevere through it.

outline.heading: The human wish to see a great person fall
outline.gist: When someone is better than us, part of us hopes they slip so we can feel we are not inferior.

outline.heading: Attacking character, not sanity
outline.gist: Opponents dig for ethical flaws because that destroys trust, while madness is shrugged off, as modern politics shows.

outline.heading: Madness was all they had
outline.gist: Had he made one ethical slip they would have used harsher words; they called him mad because he never slipped.

outline.heading: Your slip tarnishes the Prophet's legacy
outline.gist: Anyone representing Islam stands in his position; a lapse, even for a good reason, is used against the deen, since a deen without ethics is no deen.

outline.heading: He is only a reminder to the worlds
outline.gist: He takes 'it' to refer to Muhammad himself: a reminder to all of how to uphold ethics despite difficulty.

outline.heading: Interlude
Hadith: the best and purest of your deeds
outline.gist: The Prophet asked whether he should tell them of a deed better than spending gold and silver or meeting the enemy in battle.

outline.heading: The comparison is contextual
outline.gist: In famine giving matters most and under invasion defence does; in ordinary times one act surpasses them.

outline.heading: Remembrance is the essence of every deed
outline.gist: Charity or battle without Allah present in the heart means nothing; prayer itself is established for His remembrance.

outline.heading: Carry remembrance at all times
outline.gist: Whether praying, walking, studying or giving, keep Allah present; He does not need our wealth or lives but their essence.

29:36.en: And unto Midian We sent Shu'eyb, their brother. He said: O my people! Serve Allah, and look forward to the Last Day, and do not evil, making mischief, in the earth

29:37.ar: فَكَذَّبُوهُ فَأَخَذَتۡهُمُ ٱلرَّجۡفَةُ فَأَصۡبَحُواْ فِي دَارِهِمۡ جَٰثِمِينَ
29:37.en: But they denied him, and the dreadful earthquake took them, and morning found them prostrate in their dwelling place

29:38.ar: وَعَادࣰ ا وَثَمُودَاْ وَقَد تَّبَيَّنَ لَكُم مِّن مَّسَٰكِنِهِمۡۖ وَزَيَّنَ لَهُمُ ٱلشَّيۡطَٰنُ أَعۡمَٰلَهُمۡ فَصَدَّهُمۡ عَنِ ٱلسَّبِيلِ وَكَانُواْ مُسۡتَبۡصِرِينَ
29:38.en: And (the tribes of) A'ad and Thamud! (Their fate) is manifest unto you from their (ruined and deserted) dwellings. Satan made their deeds seem fair unto them and so debarred them from the Way, though they were keen observers

29:39.ar: وَقَٰرُونَ وَفِرۡعَوۡنَ وَهَٰمَٰنَۖ وَلَقَدۡ جَآءَهُم مُّوسَىٰ بِٱلۡبَيِّنَٰتِ فَٱسۡتَكۡبَرُواْ فِي ٱلۡأَرۡضِ وَمَا كَانُواْ سَٰبِقِينَ
29:39.en: And Korah, Pharaoh and Haman! Moses came unto them with clear proofs (of Allah's Sovereignty), but they were boastful in the land. And they were not winners (in the race)

29:40.ar: فَكُلًّا أَخَذۡنَا بِذَنۢبِهِۦۖ فَمِنۡهُم مَّنۡ أَرۡسَلۡنَا عَلَيۡهِ حَاصِبࣰ ا وَمِنۡهُم مَّنۡ أَخَذَتۡهُ ٱلصَّيۡحَةُ وَمِنۡهُم مَّنۡ خَسَفۡنَا بِهِ ٱلۡأَرۡضَ وَمِنۡهُم مَّنۡ أَغۡرَقۡنَاۚ وَمَا كَانَ ٱللَّهُ لِيَظۡلِمَهُمۡ وَلَٰكِن كَانُوٓاْ أَنفُسَهُمۡ يَظۡلِمُونَ
29:40.en: So We took each one in his sin; of them was he on whom We sent a hurricane, and of them was he who was overtaken by the (Awful) Cry, and of them was he whom We caused the earth to swallow, and of them was he whom We drowned. It was not for Allah to wrong them, but they wronged themselves

29:2.ar: أَحَسِبَ ٱلنَّاسُ أَن يُتۡرَكُوٓاْ أَن يَقُولُوٓاْ ءَامَنَّا وَهُمۡ لَا يُفۡتَنُونَ
29:2.en: Do men imagine that they will be left (at ease) because they say, We believe, and will not be tested with affliction

29:3.ar: وَلَقَدۡ فَتَنَّا ٱلَّذِينَ مِن قَبۡلِهِمۡۖ فَلَيَعۡلَمَنَّ ٱللَّهُ ٱلَّذِينَ صَدَقُواْ وَلَيَعۡلَمَنَّ ٱلۡكَٰذِبِينَ
29:3.en: Lo! We tested those who were before you. Thus Allah knoweth those who are sincere, and knoweth those who feign

29:6.ar: وَمَن جَٰهَدَ فَإِنَّمَا يُجَٰهِدُ لِنَفۡسِهِۦٓۚ إِنَّ ٱللَّهَ لَغَنِيٌّ عَنِ ٱلۡعَٰلَمِينَ
29:6.en: And whosoever striveth, striveth only for himself, for lo! Allah is altogether Independent of (His) creatures

22:39.ar: أُذِنَ لِلَّذِينَ يُقَٰتَلُونَ بِأَنَّهُمۡ ظُلِمُواْۚ وَإِنَّ ٱللَّهَ عَلَىٰ نَصۡرِهِمۡ لَقَدِيرٌ
22:39.en: Sanction is given unto those who fight because they have been wronged; and Allah is indeed Able to give them victory

29:10.ar: وَمِنَ ٱلنَّاسِ مَن يَقُولُ ءَامَنَّا بِٱللَّهِ فَإِذَآ أُوذِيَ فِي ٱللَّهِ جَعَلَ فِتۡنَةَ ٱلنَّاسِ كَعَذَابِ ٱللَّهِۖ وَلَئِن جَآءَ نَصۡرࣱ مِّن رَّبِّكَ لَيَقُولُنَّ إِنَّا كُنَّا مَعَكُمۡۚ أَوَلَيۡسَ ٱللَّهُ بِأَعۡلَمَ بِمَا فِي صُدُورِ ٱلۡعَٰلَمِينَ
29:10.en: Of mankind is he who saith: We believe in Allah, but, if he be made to suffer for the sake of Allah, he mistaketh the persecution of mankind for Allah's punishment; and then, if victory cometh from thy Lord, will say: Lo! we were with you (all the while). Is not Allah Best Aware of what is in the bosoms of (His) creatures

21:34.ar: وَمَا جَعَلۡنَا لِبَشَرࣲ مِّن قَبۡلِكَ ٱلۡخُلۡدَۖ أَفَإِيْن مِّتَّ فَهُمُ ٱلۡخَٰلِدُونَ
21:34.en: We appointed immortality for no mortal before thee. What! if thou diest, can they be immortal

90:2.en: And thou art an indweller of this city

89:8.ar: ٱلَّتِي لَمۡ يُخۡلَقۡ مِثۡلُهَا فِي ٱلۡبِلَٰدِ
89:8.en: The like of which was not created in the lands

89:9.en: And with (the tribe of) Thamud, who clove the rocks in the valley

14:37.ar: رَّبَّنَآ إِنِّيٓ أَسۡكَنتُ مِن ذُرِّيَّتِي بِوَادٍ غَيۡرِ ذِي زَرۡعٍ عِندَ بَيۡتِكَ ٱلۡمُحَرَّمِ رَبَّنَا لِيُقِيمُواْ ٱلصَّلَوٰةَ فَٱجۡعَلۡ أَفۡـِٔدَةࣰ مِّنَ ٱلنَّاسِ تَهۡوِيٓ إِلَيۡهِمۡ وَٱرۡزُقۡهُم مِّنَ ٱلثَّمَرَٰتِ لَعَلَّهُمۡ يَشۡكُرُونَ
14:37.en: Our Lord! Lo! I have settled some of my posterity in an uncultivable valley near unto Thy holy House, our Lord! that they may establish proper worship; so incline some hearts of men that they may yearn toward them, and provide Thou them with fruits in order that they may be thankful

11:62.ar: قَالُواْ يَٰصَٰلِحُ قَدۡ كُنتَ فِينَا مَرۡجُوࣰّ ا قَبۡلَ هَٰذَآۖ أَتَنۡهَىٰنَآ أَن نَّعۡبُدَ مَا يَعۡبُدُ ءَابَآؤُنَا وَإِنَّنَا لَفِي شَكࣲّ مِّمَّا تَدۡعُونَآ إِلَيۡهِ مُرِيبࣲ‏
11:62.en: They said: O Salih! Thou hast been among us hitherto as that wherein our hope was placed. Dost thou ask us not to worship what our fathers worshipped? Lo! we verily are in grave doubt concerning that to which thou callest us

17:90.ar: وَقَالُواْ لَن نُّؤۡمِنَ لَكَ حَتَّىٰ تَفۡجُرَ لَنَا مِنَ ٱلۡأَرۡضِ يَنۢبُوعًا
17:90.en: And they say: We will not put faith in thee till thou cause a spring to gush forth from the earth for us

17:91.ar: أَوۡ تَكُونَ لَكَ جَنَّةࣱ مِّن نَّخِيلࣲ وَعِنَبࣲ فَتُفَجِّرَ ٱلۡأَنۡهَٰرَ خِلَٰلَهَا تَفۡجِيرًا
17:91.en: Or thou have a garden of date-palms and grapes, and cause rivers to gush forth therein abundantly

17:92.ar: أَوۡ تُسۡقِطَ ٱلسَّمَآءَ كَمَا زَعَمۡتَ عَلَيۡنَا كِسَفًا أَوۡ تَأۡتِيَ بِٱللَّهِ وَٱلۡمَلَٰٓئِكَةِ قَبِيلًا
17:92.en: Or thou cause the heaven to fall upon us piecemeal, as thou hast pretended, or bring Allah and the angels as a warrant

17:93.ar: أَوۡ يَكُونَ لَكَ بَيۡتࣱ مِّن زُخۡرُفٍ أَوۡ تَرۡقَىٰ فِي ٱلسَّمَآءِ وَلَن نُّؤۡمِنَ لِرُقِيِّكَ حَتَّىٰ تُنَزِّلَ عَلَيۡنَا كِتَٰبࣰ ا نَّقۡرَؤُهُۥۗ قُلۡ سُبۡحَانَ رَبِّي هَلۡ كُنتُ إِلَّا بَشَرࣰ ا رَّسُولࣰ ا
17:93.en: Or thou have a house of gold; or thou ascend up into heaven, and even then we will put no faith in thine ascension till thou bring down for us a book that we can read. Say (O Muhammad): My Lord be Glorified! Am I aught save a mortal messenger

45:23.ar: أَفَرَءَيۡتَ مَنِ ٱتَّخَذَ إِلَٰهَهُۥ هَوَىٰهُ وَأَضَلَّهُ ٱللَّهُ عَلَىٰ عِلۡمࣲ وَخَتَمَ عَلَىٰ سَمۡعِهِۦ وَقَلۡبِهِۦ وَجَعَلَ عَلَىٰ بَصَرِهِۦ غِشَٰوَةࣰ فَمَن يَهۡدِيهِ مِنۢ بَعۡدِ ٱللَّهِۚ أَفَلَا تَذَكَّرُونَ
45:23.en: Hast thou seen him who maketh his desire his god, and Allah sendeth him astray purposely, and sealeth up his hearing and his heart, and setteth on his sight a covering? Then who will lead him after Allah (hath condemned him)? Will ye not then heed

28:76.ar: ۞إِنَّ قَٰرُونَ كَانَ مِن قَوۡمِ مُوسَىٰ فَبَغَىٰ عَلَيۡهِمۡۖ وَءَاتَيۡنَٰهُ مِنَ ٱلۡكُنُوزِ مَآ إِنَّ مَفَاتِحَهُۥ لَتَنُوٓأُ بِٱلۡعُصۡبَةِ أُوْلِي ٱلۡقُوَّةِ إِذۡ قَالَ لَهُۥ قَوۡمُهُۥ لَا تَفۡرَحۡۖ إِنَّ ٱللَّهَ لَا يُحِبُّ ٱلۡفَرِحِينَ
28:76.en: Now Korah was of Moses' folk, but he oppressed them; and We gave him so much treasure that the stores thereof would verily have been a burden for a troop of mighty men. When his own folk said unto him: Exult not; lo! Allah loveth not the exultant

r3qgleIdLaA.title: Friday Arabic Tafsir: Surat Al-Ankabut 38-40
r3qgleIdLaA.one_line: Why the prophets' trials console the Prophet, 'Ad, Thamud, Qarun and Pharaoh seized for their sins, and why Allah never wrongs anyone.
r3qgleIdLaA.summary: He recaps the surah's axis: a believer's relationship with life is mujahadah, and trials are how truthfulness and faith become visible, just as gold is known only in the furnace. He presses the audience to check whether they truly expect hardship or secretly think the rules apply to everyone but them. Reading the passage through the Prophet's eyes, he shows each story as consolation on the eve of the hijrah: Nuh stayed far longer, Ibrahim emigrated often, Lut and Shu'ayb went to worse peoples, and Quraysh were not destroyed when he left. He stresses this does not lessen the Prophet's own struggle. On 'Ad and Thamud he digresses into Adnani and Qahtani Arabs, whose distant lineage he links to lingering tribal and national contempt among Arabs today, recalling how his own village looked down on the next. Thamud were people of insight misled by luxury, illustrated by the narrated story of the she-camel demanded in mockery. The final examples are nations rather than prophets, showing that even tyrants are tested. 'Each We seized for his sin' should make us grateful we were not taken; Allah never wrongs anyone, people wrong themselves.

outline.heading: The surah's axis: life as mujahadah
outline.gist: Jihad here is broader than fighting, which was not yet permitted when this Makkan surah was revealed.

outline.heading: Trials reveal who is truthful
outline.gist: Without hardship no one could tell believer from hypocrite or friend from enemy; Umar said you do not know a man until you deal with or travel with him.

outline.heading: Gold is known only in the furnace
outline.gist: A person's metal shows when angered or wronged; expecting the religion to be easy from start to finish is naive.

outline.heading: If the prophets were tested, what of us?
outline.gist: Nuh, Ibrahim, Lut and Shu'ayb each faced a distinct hardship; no one leaves life unscratched.

outline.heading: Is this really obvious to you?
outline.gist: People bring him their problems as if no one told them life is a struggle; he urges each person to check himself.

outline.heading: Everyone wants to be the exception
outline.gist: We want others to wait at the light and queue at the bakery but excuse ourselves; if anyone were exempted, it would be the prophets.

outline.heading: The Prophet's losses
outline.gist: Orphaned of father, mother, grandfather, then losing his uncle, wife, sons, three daughters, Zayd and grandsons: why should you be spared?

outline.heading: 'We must teach the common people'
outline.gist: Whoever sees himself above the 'commoners' has no beneficial knowledge; accept for yourself the hardships you accept for others.

outline.heading: Read the Quran from the Prophet's position
outline.gist: The Quran addressed him first, then the Companions, then us; place yourself where he stood to grasp the message.

outline.heading: Revealed as he prepared to leave Makkah
outline.gist: During the pledges with Yathrib, he did not want to leave the sanctuary where he was born; the surah tells him no one is spared trials.

outline.heading: Consolation in each story
outline.gist: Nuh stayed 950 years, Ibrahim emigrated repeatedly with one follower, Lut went to a wholly corrupt people; Yathrib was a respectable people.

outline.heading: Shu'ayb's people versus the Ansar
outline.gist: Shu'ayb found a people of theft and double standards and few believers; the Prophet went to a people mostly believing in him.

outline.heading: Meaning of jathimin
outline.gist: Lying with full dead weight on the ground, as a corpse does.

outline.heading: Your people were not destroyed when you left
outline.gist: Stories detailed elsewhere are mentioned briefly here; unlike Lut's and Shu'ayb's towns, no punishment fell on Quraysh.

outline.heading: This does not diminish the Prophet's struggle
outline.gist: Some scholars avoid this framing; no one strove or was tested as he was, and the Quran was easing his burden.

outline.heading: Brief stories serve only as reminders
outline.gist: Stories that fill pages elsewhere are compressed into two verses because the aim is to remind.

outline.heading: Look at those below you
outline.gist: Seeing another's hardship lightens your own; looking upward makes you scorn Allah's blessings and add resentment to trial.

outline.heading: Recitation of 'Ad and Thamud
outline.gist: He begins the closing verses of the section.

outline.heading: Tajweed and grammar: Thamud and diptotes
outline.gist: The written alif after Thamud is not pronounced in Hafs; 'Ad takes nunation but Thamud, a foreign proper noun, does not, like Ibrahim versus Muhammad.

outline.heading: Recitation of the closing verses
outline.gist: Qarun, Pharaoh and Haman, and the four punishments.

outline.heading: 'Ad and Thamud: peoples of Hud and Salih
outline.gist: Ibn Ashur lists about ten readings of the implied verb; these are the Qahtani Arabs, wrongly called 'extinct' or 'pure' Arabs.

outline.heading: Adnani and Qahtani Arabs
outline.gist: Adnanis descend from Ismail, whose family were Canaanites from Iraq; Qahtanis likely from Hud; one language yet lineages meeting only at Nuh, unique in the world.

outline.heading: Why Arabia was never united
outline.gist: These deep divisions explain why one ruler never held the peninsula and why Arabs still fight and insult one another.

outline.heading: Residue of tribal contempt today
outline.gist: Syrians, Palestinians, Egyptians and Saudis insult each other carrying an ancient mindset they do not even understand.

outline.heading: His village and the next one
outline.gist: He was raised to see the neighbouring village as fools, then found a classmate from there wiser than anyone at home.

outline.heading: 'It has become clear to you from their dwellings'
outline.gist: Addressed to all Arabs, who knew the ruins of Al-Hijr and Al-Ahqaf, Iram of the pillars and rock-hewn homes.

outline.heading: Mustabsirin: people of insight
outline.gist: They had reason and knowledge, yet Shaytan beautified their deeds and barred them from the way.

outline.heading: Luxury makes people deaf to guidance
outline.gist: The pampered do not listen to any sermon; that is why most followers of prophets were poor.

outline.heading: Why Adnanis prospered and Qahtanis dwindled
outline.gist: 'Ad and Thamud were wiped out, while Ibrahim's prayer brought provision to his descendants around the House.

outline.heading: Salih: 'we had hopes in you'
outline.gist: His people's affluence made them mock his call to leave what their fathers worshipped.

outline.heading: The she-camel demanded in mockery
outline.gist: Drunk, they jokingly specified a camel from a rock, pregnant, drinking a whole well; Salih repeated their 'order', Allah produced it, and they slaughtered it.

outline.heading: Quraysh had more sense: Abu Sufyan
outline.gist: Most who opposed the Prophet and survived later believed; Abu Sufyan spent twenty years trying to kill him, then died fighting for Islam.

outline.heading: Quraysh's demands were not this frivolous
outline.gist: They asked for springs, gardens and a ladder to the sky, but not mockery like Thamud's.

outline.heading: Misled despite knowledge
outline.gist: They assumed their blessings would last; Shaytan can mislead a person knowingly, as with one who takes his desire as his god.

outline.heading: From prophets to nations: everyone is tested
outline.gist: The first four examples name prophets, the last name nations, showing trials fall on both the righteous and the corrupt.

outline.heading: Even choosing Pharaoh's life gives no escape
outline.gist: Some live by trampling others as 'fair game for the clever', yet even they are tested and struck.

outline.heading: You only choose your stance before Allah
outline.gist: Belief or disbelief, you will be tested; truthfulness turns the trial to good, lying turns it to evil.

outline.heading: Qarun, Pharaoh and Haman: unchecked power
outline.gist: Wealth whose keys burdened a band of men, rule over people, and power to kill at will, yet they could not outrun Allah.

outline.heading: 'Each We seized for his sin'
outline.gist: Scholars tremble at this phrase; we sit here safely only because Allah has not seized us for our sins.

outline.heading: Quraysh spared, and the Prophet's fear for Makkah
outline.gist: He feared his people would meet the fate of earlier nations; Allah did not destroy them at Badr, Uhud or the Trench.

outline.heading: The ummah will not be destroyed from outside
outline.gist: Allah promised not to destroy it by general famine or an outside enemy, unless Muslims destroy each other: the problem and solution lie in their hands.

outline.heading: Four punishments in the order of the nations
outline.gist: Stone-wind for 'Ad, the blast for Thamud, the earth swallowing Qarun, drowning for Pharaoh and Haman.

outline.heading: Allah would never wrong them
outline.gist: 'Allah was not one to wrong them' means injustice is impossible for Him; He created people to love and be loved, and they wronged themselves.

outline.heading: You write your own book
outline.gist: Each person's deeds lead him to his destination; Allah treats us with beauty while we answer with ugliness.

outline.heading: Outro
